raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39592/files) against `main`.

dLLM prefix lookup can consume a partial prompt block and its synthetic masks when a cached prompt contains the same literal mask IDs. Literal mask IDs in a real prompt can also be denoised and emitted as generated tokens, causing KV accounting errors and a serving crash.

Bound cache lookup by complete real-token blocks and classify the request after matching its cache prefix. Carry an explicit committed-position mask into LowConfidence, JointThreshold and JointThresholdInDel so literal prompt IDs and previously emitted outputs stay immutable after retraction. Repeated denoising no longer subtracts the current block from the reported cached-token count. The change preserves autoregressive lookup and logprob boundaries.

The GPU/HTTP results below are historical qualification of the previous revision; they were not rerun for the October 10 refresh.

| Test | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real RadixCache collision, five prompt tokens with block size 4 | Matches 8 tokens and skips the tail | Matches 4; tail preserved |
| SDAR HTTP prompt containing a literal mask in a full block | Service exits with KV pool overcount on baseline and initial lookup-only patch | Cold/hot requests complete; prompt remains intact |
| Prefix boundary, FDFO KV reuse, and literal-prompt algorithm regressions | Original boundary matrix: 122 failures out of 210 | 11 tests and 228 subtests pass |
| LowConfidence, FDFO, radix enabled | — | 8 prompt cases plus synthetic-mask collision pass |
| LowConfidence, explicitly synchronous (`--no-dllm-fdfo`) | — | Same 9 cases pass; exact output IDs/text match FDFO |
| LowConfidence, FDFO, radix disabled | — | Same 9 cases pass; exact output IDs/text match cache-enabled run |
| JointThreshold, FDFO, radix enabled | — | Same 9 cases pass; cold/hot IDs/text identical |
| JointThreshold, explicitly synchronous | — | Same 9 cases pass; exact IDs/text match JointThreshold FDFO |
| HTTP cached-token accounting | Negative counts during repeated denoising | Nonnegative and equal to the first traced prefix match |

HTTP tests use `JetLM/SDAR-1.7B-Chat-b32`, BF16, TP=1, Triton, CUDA graphs disabled, block size 32, threshold 0.95, greedy sampling, 32 new tokens, and `ignore_eos=true`. Hardware: RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24 GB; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.7. Each configuration runs 19 actual `/generate` requests. An observation-only wrapper records cache matches after `Req.init_next_round_input`.

| Prompt length | Expected hot cache hit | Radix-disabled hit |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 31 | 0 | 0 |
| 32 | 32 | 0 |
| 33 | 32 | 0 |
| 63 | 32 | 0 |
| 64 | 64 | 0 |
| 65 | 64 | 0 |
| 129 | 128 | 0 |
| 65, including literal mask ID | 64 | 0 |

The collision test first caches a 33-token prompt followed by 31 literal mask IDs, then submits the original 33-token prompt. Its output matches a clean-cache request and only 32 tokens are reused. Unit tests additionally exercise both JointThreshold implementations and both scheduling modes. These results do not qualify CUDA graph execution or multi-block prefill.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py \
  test/registered/unit/dllm/algorithm/test_joint_threshold_indel.py \
  test/registered/unit/dllm/test_gemma4_renoise.py
```

Contributes to the prefix-cache / prompt-tail item in #39499. The post-cache phase ordering overlaps the prerequisite in #31586; this PR does not add its multi-block scheduler.

### October 10 review follow-up

Merged main `c55790d38ba0c41170cec8993e7a85d5c687149c` and addressed the remaining review items:

- Batch CPU-known committed lengths into the same pinned, nonblocking transfer as positions. LowConfidence uses `torch.where` to exclude committed positions. Algorithms read the declared ForwardBatch field directly, and test doubles provide it explicitly.
- Retraction phase selection and position masks include both prompt tokens and committed outputs, independently of KV residency.
- JointThresholdInDel uses the explicit immutable mask for state initialization and excludes those positions from mask counts and transfers, while retaining its contiguous-prefix fallback when metadata is absent.
- Existing registered CPU test files now contain regressions for a literal-mask cache collision, immutable literal prompts in synchronous/FDFO decoding, retracted outputs, repeated-pass cached-token accounting and InDel behavior.

All scoped pre-commit checks passed, including CI registry validation. CPU source execution passed 25 exact repository algorithm tests, committed-token phase/prefix controls over 72 prompt/output layouts, three actual position-branch controls and the repeated-pass cache-accounting guard. Negative controls reproduced the literal-prompt InDel failure; these tests also caught and corrected its mask-count/transfer path. This source-level run omits package initialization and native dependencies. Full registered-suite and HTTP reruns require the complete SGLang environment and were not executed in this refresh; no GPU performance or memory measurement is claimed.

nodes.body: On current main, a prompt holding the mask id still kills the scheduler under `JointThresholdInDel`, which ignores `dllm_prompt_mask`. Consider taking its prompt positions and original masks from that mask when it is set.
With the regression tests removed, no CI test fails on main for the literal prompt mask, the prefix bound, or negative cached tokens. Could you add one case for each to the existing dLLM tests?

Thanks, folding the prompt lengths into the existing transfer removes the sync. Could we build `dllm_prompt_mask` only for batches where a request’s last partial prompt block holds the mask id, so ordinary batches skip the extra bytes and kernel?

Building `prompt_lens` with `device=device` adds a blocking copy and stream sync to every dLLM forward, with or without literal masks. Could we send the lengths in the existing non-blocking positions transfer instead?

The in-place `&=` with `~prompt_mask` lazily loads two bool kernels LowConfidence never ran before, adding about 48 MiB to every scheduler process. Consider `torch.where(prompt_mask, False, block_mask_index)`, which yields the same mask without them.

`dllm_prompt_mask` is a declared `ForwardBatch` field, while sglang code reads always-present fields directly instead of probing with `getattr`. Consider reading the attribute directly and setting it in the test fakes.

A retracted request keeps `output_ids`, so its resumed block of prompt tail plus old outputs would read as decode and re-emit them. Consider keying the phase and prompt mask on the committed length instead.

+            origin_input_ids=array("q", prompt),
+            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_new_tokens=16, temperature=0),
+            vocab_size=128,
+            dllm_config=DllmConfig("LowConfidence", {}, 4, 99, 4),
+        )
+        req.output_ids.extend(output)
+        return req
+
+    def test_cache_lookup_stops_before_partial_prompt_and_synthetic_masks(self):
+        # A different request legitimately cached these literal mask IDs. Only
+        # the first complete block belongs to this request's committed prefix.
+        cache = RadixCache.create_simulated(page_size=4)
+        cache.insert(
+            InsertParams(
+                key=RadixKey(array("q", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 99, 99, 99])),
+                value=torch.arange(8),
+            )
+        )
+        req = self.make_req([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
+        req.init_next_round_input(cache)
+        self.assertEqual(req.prefix_len, 4)
+        self.assertEqual(req.dllm_block_offset, 4)
+        self.assertFalse(req.is_dllm_prefill())
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.full_untruncated_fill_ids[4:8]), [5, 99, 99, 99])
+
+    def test_retraction_reencodes_committed_outputs_before_denoising(self):
+        req = self.make_req([1, 99, 2], [7, 99, 8, 9, 10])
+        req.reset_for_retract()
+        req.init_next_round_input()
+        self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids), [7, 99, 8, 9, 10])
+        self.assertTrue(req.is_dllm_prefill())
+        # The second complete block consists of already-emitted output tokens.
+        req.prefix_len = 4
+        req.determine_dllm_phase()
+        self.assertTrue(req.is_dllm_prefill())
+        req.prefix_len = 8
+        req.determine_dllm_phase()
+        self.assertFalse(req.is_dllm_prefill())
+
+    def test_repeated_denoise_passes_do_not_subtract_cache_hits(self):
+        req = self.make_req([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
+        req._init_fill_ids_for_dllm()
+        req.prefix_len = 4
+        req.extend_end = 8
+        req.already_computed = 8
+        req.cached_tokens = 4
+        req._cache_breakdown_computed = True
+        batch = ScheduleBatch(
+            reqs=[req],
+            device="cpu",
+            dllm_config=req.dllm_config,
+            model_config=SimpleNamespace(is_encoder_decoder=False, vocab_size=128),
+        )
+        execution = SimpleNamespace(
+            features=SimpleNamespace(enable_encoder_swa_bounded_replay=False),
+            mamba=SimpleNamespace(enable_mamba_extra_buffer=False),
+        )
+        # Allocation and sampling are collaborators; exercise the scheduler's
+        # real cache accounting on two revisits of the same fixed-size block.
+        with (
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch.get_exec", return_value=execution
+            ),
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch.alloc_for_extend",
+                return_value=(torch.arange(4), torch.tensor([0]), torch.tensor([0])),
+            ),
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch.SamplingBatchInfo.from_schedule_batch"
+            ),
+        ):
+            for _ in range(2):
+                batch.prepare_for_extend()
+                self.assertEqual(req.cached_tokens, 4)
+
+    def test_literal_prompt_masks_are_preserved_and_not_emitted(self):
+        class Runner:
+            def forward(self, batch, **kwargs):
+                logits = torch.zeros(4, 16)
+                logits[:, 7] = 20
+                return SimpleNamespace(
+                    logits_output=SimpleNamespace(full_logits=logits),
+                    can_run_graph=False,
+                )
+
+        for cls, vectorized in (
+            (LowConfidence, False),
+            (JointThreshold, False),
+            (JointThreshold, True),
+        ):
+            for fdfo in (False, True):
+                with self.subTest(
+                    algorithm=cls.__name__, vectorized=vectorized, fdfo=fdfo
+                ):
+                    algorithm = cls(
+                        DllmConfig(
+                            cls.__name__,
+                            {"vectorized_decoding": vectorized},
+                            4,
+                            15,
+                            1,
+                            fdfo,
+                        )
+                    )
+                    batch = SimpleNamespace(
+                        batch_size=1,
+                        input_ids=torch.tensor([15, 2, 15, 15]),
+                        dllm_prompt_mask=torch.tensor([[True, True, False, False]]),
+                    )
+                    states = None
+                    for _ in range(32):
+                        _, output, accepted, states, _ = algorithm.run(
+                            Runner(), batch, states
+                        )
+                        self.assertEqual(batch.input_ids[:2].tolist(), [15, 2])
+                        if not fdfo or accepted == [4]:
+                            break
+                    else:
+                        self.fail("denoising did not finish")
+                    self.assertEqual(batch.input_ids.tolist(), [15, 2, 7, 7])
+                    if not fdfo:
+                        self.assertEqual(output[0].tolist(), [7, 7])
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

inline_comments.body: Building `prompt_lens` with `device=device` adds a blocking copy and stream sync to every dLLM forward, with or without literal masks. Could we send the lengths in the existing non-blocking positions transfer instead?

The in-place `&=` with `~prompt_mask` lazily loads two bool kernels LowConfidence never ran before, adding about 48 MiB to every scheduler process. Consider `torch.where(prompt_mask, False, block_mask_index)`, which yields the same mask without them.

`dllm_prompt_mask` is a declared `ForwardBatch` field, while sglang code reads always-present fields directly instead of probing with `getattr`. Consider reading the attribute directly and setting it in the test fakes.

A retracted request keeps `output_ids`, so its resumed block of prompt tail plus old outputs would read as decode and re-emit them. Consider keying the phase and prompt mask on the committed length instead.

issue_comments.body: On current main, a prompt holding the mask id still kills the scheduler under `JointThresholdInDel`, which ignores `dllm_prompt_mask`. Consider taking its prompt positions and original masks from that mask when it is set.
With the regression tests removed, no CI test fails on main for the literal prompt mask, the prefix bound, or negative cached tokens. Could you add one case for each to the existing dLLM tests?

Thanks, folding the prompt lengths into the existing transfer removes the sync. Could we build `dllm_prompt_mask` only for batches where a request’s last partial prompt block holds the mask id, so ordinary batches skip the extra bytes and kernel?
